date: # Events around FOMC decisions: the shock or data the Fed was reacting to. emergency = yes for a move between scheduled meetings.
# Decisions themselves are computed from the target range; add the context of any new decision here (the 2026 hike has none yet).

event: Last hike of the 2004-06 cycle, to 5.25%; US house prices peaking.
BNP Paribas freezes three funds exposed to US subprime mortgages; money markets seize up.
First cut, 50 bp, as subprime losses spread to banks.
Emergency 75 bp cut between meetings after a global stock sell-off.
Bear Stearns rescued by JPMorgan with Fed support; 75 bp cut two days later.
Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy; AIG rescued the next day.
Coordinated 50 bp cut with the ECB, BoE and others, between meetings.
QE1 announced: purchases of agency debt and mortgage-backed securities.
Target cut to a 0-0.25% range: the zero lower bound.
QE2: $600bn of longer-term Treasuries.
S&P downgrades the US from AAA to AA+ after the debt-ceiling standoff.
Operation Twist: sell short Treasuries, buy long ones.
QE3: open-ended MBS purchases, later Treasuries too.
Bernanke hints at slowing purchases: the 'taper tantrum' lifts the 10-year by about 1 point by September.
Lift-off: first hike since 2006, to 0.25-0.5%.
Balance-sheet runoff (QT1) begins.
Fourth hike of 2018 into a falling stock market; the Fed turns 'patient' a month later.
First cut since 2008: 'insurance' against the trade war and slowing growth.
Repo-market rates spike to 10%: reserves had become scarce; the Fed starts buying bills.
Emergency 50 bp cut as Covid spreads.
Emergency cut to 0-0.25% and $700bn of purchases (a Sunday).
Taper of Covid-era purchases announced; inflation above 6%.
Lift-off with CPI near 8% after Russia invades Ukraine.
75 bp hike, the largest since 1994, after an 8.6% CPI print.
Silicon Valley Bank fails; the Fed still hikes 25 bp on 22 March.
Last hike of the cycle, to 5.25-5.5%, a 22-year high.
First cut of the cycle, 50 bp, as unemployment rises.
Broad US tariffs announced; markets sell off and Treasury yields jump.

Cut, and the end of balance-sheet runoff announced for 1 December.
